summary: Milestone 2026.10.719 completed 9 experiments (1 compute-bound, 8 synthesis-only) across 41.7 total wall-time minutes (averaging 5 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was led by synthesis-only tasks accounting for four of the top 5 slowest runs—qualifying local updates with independent arithmetic and real restart controls (8.12 minutes), reconciling fourteen outcomes with bounded historical memory (6.3 minutes), qualifying current source custody (5.07 minutes), and covering ARC reader failure branches (4.91 minutes)—alongside the sole compute-bound task qualifying versioned runtime evidence (4.83 minutes). With gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false, the point-in-time monitor reading of 0% GPU utilization (2MB allocated) on the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 reflects expected idle state for non-GPU synthesis workloads, and single-model runtime qualification correctly avoided multi-model DualGPURunner dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis-only tasks accounted for the vast majority of milestone wall time (8 of 9 completed experiments, and four of the top five slowest runs totaling 24.4 minutes out of 41.7 total wall-time minutes), led by local update qualification (8.12 minutes) and fourteen-outcome reconciliation (6.3 minutes).

The sole compute-bound task ('Qualify versioned runtime evidence independently and require a real CUDA change') required 4.83 minutes, but individual experiment receipts lack granular intra-task sub-phase telemetry (environment probing, CUDA initialization, evidence validation, result serialization) to diagnose internal latency.

Synthesis tasks executed serially across local update qualification, source custody checks, ARC reader branch coverage, and fourteen-outcome reconciliation without incremental receipt caching or evidence memoization when upstream artifacts remained unchanged.
Milestone timing analysis relied on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction due to the live git-log path finding 0 commits in the milestone interval.
improvements_suggested: Implement incremental receipt caching and evidence memoization for local update qualification, source custody qualification, ARC reader checks, and fourteen-outcome reconciliation when upstream inputs remain static.
Instrument multi-minute synthesis and compute-bound tasks with granular intra-phase execution timers (dependency verification, execution, serialization) to identify specific latency bottlenecks.
Persist explicit synchronous execution timestamps (start, completion, duration) directly into experiment receipt artifacts to prevent dependence on disk-mtime fallback reconstruction.
Sample continuous in-flight accelerator utilization and memory metrics during compute-bound execution intervals rather than relying solely on post-run point-in-time GPU monitor polling.
Maintain strict DualGPURunner dispatch criteria restricted to concurrent multi-model pipelines, avoiding unnecessary invocation overhead for single-model or runtime qualification workloads.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Deploy incremental receipt caching and evidence memoization for local update qualification, ARC reader checks, and outcome reconciliation when upstream artifacts are unchanged.
Instrument long-running synthesis tasks and compute-bound runtime qualification with granular intra-task phase timers.
Persist explicit synchronous start and completion lifecycle timestamps in experiment receipts and capture continuous in-flight accelerator telemetry during active runs.
meta_reflection: Across 9 completed experiments and 41.7 minutes of milestone wall time, execution duration was primarily driven by synthesis-only tasks averaging 5 minutes per experiment, led by local update qualification (8.12 minutes) and outcome reconciliation (6.3 minutes), alongside a single 4.83-minute compute-bound runtime qualification task. Point-in-time GPU monitoring showed 0% utilization on the RTX 3090 as expected for non-GPU synthesis workloads, with gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false. Operational improvements should focus on incremental receipt caching for unchanged upstream dependencies and intra-phase telemetry for multi-minute tasks, with estimated time savings conservatively kept at 0% until empirically validated.
